name: soft chipped bites of dirt in the north-east, north-west, south-west corners of one old asphalt road tile, rounding off the inside corners where roads meet at a junction: irregular quarter-blobs of dirt about 4 px across with broken lighter asphalt edges (or dry dark ledges on their south sides), loose asphalt crumbs on the dirt and dirt flecks on the road; transparent elsewhere, shown on a real T junction or crossing
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt-in-ne-nw-sw

refSet.reason: 칩셋 wasteland_ruins 의 화풍 기준 묶음이 없다

surfaces.part: dirt ground fill with asphalt T-junction shape

answer.evidence: The tile is fully opaque (width 144 on every row) and drawn straight from above. Brown dirt covers it with a grey asphalt cross or T shape, which has crumbs and flecks. The only edge detail is a few 1-2 row dark ledges on south sides (around rows 76-77, 93-94 and 124), which are thin ledge lines and not a vertical front face. No front face of 3 or more rows, no eave and no ellipse. It is a flat decal, so top_down_slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has about 4 lightness steps per material: dirt in mid, light fleck, dark fleck and shadow ledge, and asphalt in mid grey, darker grey, light crumbs and a dark edge. That is a little under Beodeul's 5-6, but close to the grass reference's roughly 4. Measured facts support it: 5 visible tones per tile against 3 for the grass and 7 for the paving, 2% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels. The edges are therefore tinted, with dark brown where the road meets dirt, not a black sticker outline. The dirt carries scattered grain and flecks, and the asphalt has crumbs and speckle, so large areas are not flat fills. Weaker points: only 9 distinct colours overall, and the speckle is fairly uniform and random rather than shaded clump by clump as in the references. As a simple transition overlay it holds up next to the grass reference, though not at the richness of the paving.

The only vertical-looking detail is 1-2 rows of dark ledge under the south edges, at about rows 76, 93 and 124. Those are thin edge shadows, not a front face of 3 or more rows. No eave, no ellipse and no receding side face are drawn, so it reads as a flat decal and not a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate shows 5 visible tones per tile, against 3 for the grass reference and 7 for the paving reference, so it sits between them. Near-flat coverage is 2%, close to the references' 0%, and the board shows no large flat areas. The dirt has grain, with light and dark flecks and crumbs. The asphalt has mottled speckle and lighter broken edges. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the edges lean brown or grey-brown and read as the dark tone of the neighbouring material, not a black sticker line. Each material has only about 4 lightness steps against Beodeul's 5-6, and the whole piece uses just 9 colours, so it is a little simpler than the paving reference. It is still at or above the grass reference on the primary facts, with tinted edges and real grain.
